soundness_flags.one_line: The statistic inf_{η∈Nδ} distance equals distance to cl(Nδ), so it necessarily admits excluded rank-loss closure points; strict CAD inequalities cannot make this an exact nonclosed-null distance test.

source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 4.1 identifies ATT(g,t) and permits comparison-group weighted averages; Theorem 4.2 supplies the influence representation, asymptotic normality, and minimum-variance GMM aggregation.
The paper’s delta-method and resampling framework assumes a Hadamard directionally differentiable map.
The numerical-delta method gives consistent inference for directionally differentiable functions and uniform validity for specified convex Lipschitz functions.

source_verification_receipts.version: Author-hosted Journal of Econometrics accepted-manuscript version, 2020
source_verification_receipts.locator: pp. 4–5, Assumption A1 and subsequence discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper provides a subsequence-based framework for establishing asymptotic size and coverage.
The paper develops SR-AR and SR-CQLR procedures robust to weak identification and near/exact singular moment covariance, with asymptotic-size results.
For nondifferentiable targets, the paper rules out locally asymptotically unbiased and alpha-quantile-unbiased estimator sequences.
The cited article exists as Double/debiased machine learning for treatment and structural parameters and concerns orthogonal-score inference with cross-fitting.
Asymptotic Statistics by A. W. van der Vaart was published by Cambridge University Press in 1998.
Chen and Fang publish an inference procedure specifically for matrix rank, making it a closer missing comparator for rank-loss behavior.
